title: Financial Times: US ports face a surge in attempted cyberattacks, Anadolu Agency relays
date_note: The Financial Times report appeared on Sunday 22 November, according to Anadolu Agency's article of the same day; the page gives no earlier date for the report.
summary: The Financial Times reported on Sunday that US ports face a surge in attempted cyberattacks, Anadolu Agency relays. According to the report, the Port of Corpus Christi in Texas is experiencing hundreds or even thousands of attempted cyberattacks daily, and its CEO Kent Britton said hackers were probing networks and impersonating senior executives. The Port of Los Angeles reported blocking 120 million attempted cyberattacks in August, the report says.
plain: A Financial Times report relayed by Anadolu says US ports face many attempted cyberattacks; the Port of Los Angeles reported blocking 120 million attempted cyberattacks in August.
exec: According to the FT report, attackers are probing US port networks and impersonating senior executives.

sources.name: Central News Agency via money.udn.com (relaying the Financial Times)

evidence.quote: The Port of Los Angeles reported blocking 120 million attempted cyberattacks in August, nearly twice its monthly average in 2023, while the US Coast Guard recorded a 17% increase in maritime cyber incidents last year.

validation.note: Anadolu Agency and Taiwan's Central News Agency (via money.udn.com) both relay the same Financial Times report, so it is one underlying report. The FT article (paywalled) was not read; The Hill and Traders Union answered 403 and wn.com could not be fetched.

review.note: Compared title, date 22 Nov, Corpus Christi, Port of LA 120 million and evidence quote against Anadolu and CNA; single_source fits
